subject: Pelotonix Dedicated: surge slab recommendation, tokens/sec mapping, and SLO fit

Cc: lucia.gomez <lucia.gomez@pelotonix.ai>
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood Dedicated sizing: tokens/sec + SLA fit for PX POC

Olga / Ben —

Quick context: Pelotonix is starting a 6-week POC (intent to move to committed Dedicated if tests hit performance targets). Procurement wants a one-page summary showing expected tokens/sec, p95 latency at target load, and recommended committed slab with headroom. Key constraints: 1) target p95 <= 400ms for responses up to ~200 tokens, 2) spike protection for +3x baseline for the first two weeks of launch.

Do you have a short capacity model and recommended slab (GPU count / equivalent) we can attach to the MAA? Also need an approximate committed monthly token run-rate tied to pricing so our CFO can run the numbers.

Thanks —
Samir
Samir Shah
Head of Platform
Pelotonix

From: olga_petrov <olga@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood Dedicated sizing: tokens/sec + SLA fit for PX POC

Samir — thanks for the clear ask. Attaching a compact capacity sheet (see 'pelotonix_capacity_model_v2.xlsx') and a short executive summary below. I kept numbers conservative so procurement has margin.

Executive summary (short):
- Workload profile: Mainly chat completions and short-context instructions; median response length ~140 tokens, 95th percentile ~380 tokens. Live inference uses Llama2-13B (quantized) as the baseline; we propose SuperL2-13B-Opt for production rollouts where lower latency is critical.
- Per-GPU throughput guidance (typical, measured on our Dedicated stack):
  • Baseline model (q4_13b) ~ 600 tokens/sec per GPU at batching=8 for short responses (median length 140).
  • Optimized variant (superl2-13b-opt) ~ 820 tokens/sec per GPU under similar conditions (better kernel & KV cache behavior).
  • Tail behavior: for 95th percentile lengths (~380 tokens), per-GPU sustainable throughput drops ~35% compared to median.
- SLO fit and recommended slab:
  • Target steady-state baseline (expected average load): 1,200 tokens/sec aggregate.
  • Recommended committed slab: 3 GPUs (equivalent H100-class), providing ~2,460 tokens/sec aggregate on the optimized variant (3 * 820). That gives ~2x baseline headroom for steady-state and ~1.3x at 95th-percentile token lengths after conservative degradation.
  • For spike protection (+3x initial launch spike), add a burst buffer (reserved burst pool) or short-term autoscale to 9 GPU-equivalents for the first two weeks; cost-effective vs long-term commit.
- Latency expectations:
  • With the 3-GPU slab and batching policy tuned for low-latency (max batch 8, prefer stream-first), p95 single-response latency is expected <= 350ms for median-length responses. p99 will depend on concurrent bursts; built-in fallback to smaller model (q4_7b) reduces p99 by ~60ms.

I've put the per-slot math into the spreadsheet (tab 'per_gpu_math') and added a simple monthly token run-rate tied to conversion scenarios. Let me know if you'd prefer different headroom (50% vs 100%) and I'll regenerate the scenario table.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@pelotonix.ai>, olga_petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, contracts@pelotonix.ai
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 11:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood Dedicated sizing: tokens/sec + SLA fit for PX POC

Samir / Olga — adding the commercial angle and proposed committed configuration for the MAA. Procurement asked us to bind a committed GPU count + monthly token floor to the pilot. A few details:

- Pricing snapshot (high level): committed slab (3 GPU-equivalents) + burst pool as suggested. We can price the committed slab at a blended monthly rate and allow 30% burst credits in month 1 at no extra charge. Specifics in attached 'redwood-dedicated-pricing.pdf'.
- Why 3 GPUs: With Olga's numbers, 3 GPU-equivalents cover expected avg load (1,200 tps) with ~100% headroom at median lengths and comfortable p95 latency. It also keeps the committed footprint small enough for a POC conversion.
- Token/month guidance (conservative): if you run 1,200 tokens/sec sustained for 30 days => ~3.1B tokens/month. If you need 2x baseline, scale to 6 GPUs or commit to burst capacity; we modeled alternate commitments in the sheet.
- Operational runbook highlights:
  • Warm-up: pre-warm KV cache before production traffic (30–60 min warm-up recommended).
  • Fallbacks: auto-fallback to q4_7b for tail latency events and region-level fallback to eu-us pair in case of regional capacity pressure.
  • Observability: we will provide per-route token/latency dashboards and a short alerting playbook.

If Pelotonix signs the MAA with the 3-GPU commit, I'll follow up with a simple PO template and a 30-day trial extension clause for the first month.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — procurement at Pelotonix (contracts@pelotonix.ai) + Samir: adding our standard PO template and the SOW appendix that ties a committed slab to the service levels. See attachments in this thread.

Next steps for Pelotonix procurement:
1) Review attached pricing PDF + capacity workbook.
2) Confirm whether the 30% burst credit for month 1 is acceptable; if yes, we issue a revised MAA with that clause.
3) Once MAA countersigned, we schedule the onboarding call (30–45 minutes) focused on KV cache warm-up, DOs/Don'ts for cold-start, and opt-in SLO alerting.

If Samir wants, we can push a short one-slide summary of the capacity math (for CFO) by EOD today.

Cheers,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Contracts | Redwood Inference
